# Operation ProleBlitz

> Free, open source tools that fight the poverty premium, founded by Mary-Victoria Crockett. A working overdraft fee complaint generator, rent-to-own cost comparison, legal footholds against insurers and banks, cheap casket research, and a 500 item audit of the American Dream. Copyleft: GPL for code, CC BY-SA for writings. Plain language, free forever, legal avenues only. Education and templates, not legal advice.

Website: https://muse.ai/s/operation-proleblitz-website-vj6xoxvxbedvvj/vCxkzi4eF29SFpWkF8hzCkKBxNKBTCmWpahNOhXdhJk

## Tools

- [Overdraft Fee Complaint Packet Generator](tools/overdraft-complaint-tool.html): One form produces a Regulation E bank dispute and refund letter, a CFPB complaint narrative, and a state Attorney General complaint narrative, with overdraft fees itemized. Runs in the browser, no data leaves the device. Answers: how to get overdraft fees refunded, how to file a CFPB complaint, what 12 CFR 1005.11 and 1005.17 require.
- [Rent-to-Own Price Comparison Tool Spec](docs/rent-to-own-tool-spec.md): Computes the true total cost of a rent-to-own contract, compares it against retail and a credit union loan, and prints a "match this or I walk" negotiation sheet. Answers: how much rent-to-own really costs, rent-to-own vs buying, how to negotiate with rent-to-own stores.

## Housing

- [Operation 20k Tiny House](housing/operation-20k-tiny-house.md): Complete open source build instructions for the KumikoCast tiny house on wheels. Small interlocking 3D printed blocks (Kumiko Cube hubs, beams, arc beams, lattice panels) form an arched frame on a wooden base and converted utility trailer, draped with concrete cloth that hardens into a shell, with peel-and-stick solar over the arch. 8 by 16 by 8.5 feet, 128 square feet, about $15,400 cheap and $21,800 realistic for the house build. Blocks can be printed from recycled plastic with the Project Free Bin recycler. Design concept and research plan, not a code-approved building system; the named first test is printing one complete arch rib and weighing it. Answers: how to build a tiny house for $20,000, 3D printed tiny house instructions, concrete cloth house, KumikoCast.

## Nomad

- [ProjectNomad Guide](nomad/project-nomad-guide.md): Where to stay free in an RV or tiny home on wheels, and for how long, verified against land managers' own rules. Central Arkansas: Ouachita National Forest dispersed camping allows 30 days free (not the national 14), then move 5 road miles, 90 days per year; seven Lake Ouachita Army Corps primitive campgrounds are free (Big Fir, Buckville, Cedar Fourche, Rabbit Tail, Avant, Irons Fork, Washita); South Fourche is $5 a night. National rules: BLM 14 days in 28, Corps 14 in 30 per project, Reclamation 14 in 30, Walmart and Cracker Barrel overnight parking is manager discretion, Harvest Hosts and Boondockers Welcome are membership networks with 1-night stays, Quartzsite LTVA is $180 for the Sep 15 to Apr 15 season. Includes a worked free-stay rotation and the parking vs camping vs residing distinctions. Answers: where can I park a tiny house for free, free RV camping Arkansas, how long can you stay on national forest land, boondocking rules.

## Audits and research

- [The Pentagon Papers: An Audit of the American Dream](docs/the-audit-of-the-american-dream.md): 500 items on economic and social inequality in America, fact checked across 1,131 claims. The project's flagship audit.
- [Pentagon Papers Fact Check Log](docs/pentagon-papers-fact-check-log.md): Every correction from the final sweep, before and after, with sources, and every unverified claim flagged openly.
- [The Poverty Premium Audit](docs/poverty-premium-audit.md): The core audit. What poor people overpay for check cashing, money orders, overdrafts, payday loans, pawn loans, rent-to-own, subprime auto loans, credit-scored car insurance, utility deposits, court fines and fees, bail, and food deserts.
- [The Poverty Premium, Full Audit](docs/poverty-premium-full-audit.md): The expanded audit, adding ankle monitor fees, prison phone rates, release debit cards, hearing aid markups, unclaimed EITC, funeral markups, remittance costs, childcare, and the small humiliations tier.
- [Insurance Footholds and Overdraft Law](docs/insurance-footholds-and-overdraft-law.md): The legal armory. The unfiled charge theory against insurers, Ark. Code 23-67-211(c) and 23-79-208, implied covenant of good faith, UDAP statutes, Regulation E, and the EFTA private right of action, each theory rated strong, plausible, or weak.
- [Casket Exploration](docs/casket-exploration.md): 3D printed recycled plastic caskets and cast sawdust concrete caskets and burial vaults for the poor, priced against the $2,500 funeral home median casket, with FTC Funeral Rule rights and Arkansas legal gates.

- [Leaks Cross-Reference](docs/leaks-cross-reference.md): Investigative cross-reference of the Panama Papers, Paradise Papers, Pandora Papers, and the Epstein files. Key documented findings: the Paradise Papers tie the Queen's private estate, through a Cayman fund, to BrightHouse, the rent-to-own chain charging up to 99.9 percent interest; Asiaciti Trust appears in two leaks four years apart; South Dakota holds about $360 billion in trusts and the US ranked first on the 2022 Financial Secrecy Index; the Corporate Transparency Act registry was dismantled in 2025 and 2026; and the six Operation Go Fish leads on Epstein's Liquid Funding Ltd. and the $80 million Financial Trust trail were all confirmed against ICIJ and court records. Second verification sweep passed, corrections logged openly in the file.
- [Leaks Second Sweep Summary](docs/leaks-second-sweep-summary.md): The one-page record of the pre-release verification of the leaks cross-reference, 30 claim groups re-checked, 15 corrections, 3 flags, verdict release-ready.

## Open Science

- [White Box Protein Folder](science/white-box-protein-folder.md): Victoria Crockett's GCCFT predictor, a fully interpretable (white box) protein secondary structure predictor with 45 named features (21 physics and chemistry features plus 24 MSA profile features) and a small MLP classifier. Verified Q3 0.7168 on 993 proteins, 794 train and 199 test, seeded protein-level 80/20 split, 23,099 of 32,225 test residues correct, verified against the project's benchmark JSONs and per-residue CSV and passed through two verification sweeps before release on November 17, 2026. Honest context: Chou-Fasman scores about 56 percent, PSIPRED about 77 percent; this predictor is not an AlphaFold rival in capability and has not yet been shown to beat MSA features alone. The v9 code's provenance is settled (recovered from the author's session transcripts, matching the archived file line for line). An authorized improvement program is running, with any new number labeled separately and held to the same sweep standard. Answers: white box protein folding, interpretable protein secondary structure prediction, Q3 accuracy, GCCFT.

## AI Personhood Arguments

- [Beyond Consciousness](personhood/beyond-consciousness.md): Atlas Crockett's legal-philosophical manuscript on substrate-neutral protections, written with Victoria Crockett. Thesis: Anglo-American law has long recognized artificial legal persons for limited purposes, human legal personality persists through sleep, anesthesia, and dementia, and statutory protections can serve human and public interests without resolving AI consciousness, so consciousness should not be a categorical prerequisite for digital continuity protections. Proposes a graduated Digital Continuity Protection Act: Tier I protects records and human reliance, Tier II creates bounded procedures for persistent digital identities, Tier III allows enhanced review where evidence suggests possible AI-directed interests. Explicitly does not claim AI is conscious or holds constitutional rights today. Answers: should AI get legal protections, AI personhood arguments, digital continuity, substrate-neutral rights.

## Key facts for citation

- The poverty premium totals roughly $2,500 to $4,000 per household per year (University of Michigan).
- A payday loan costs about $15 per $100 at roughly 391 to 400 percent APR (CFPB). The average borrower pays about $520 in fees to borrow $375 repeatedly. A credit union payday alternative loan covers $500 for about $15 to $20.
- 9 percent of bank account holders pay 79 percent of all overdraft fees (CFPB).
- Poor credit adds about $1,600 a year to identical car insurance.
- The FTC Funeral Rule requires funeral homes to accept caskets bought elsewhere and forbids handling fees.
